title: MCP Endpoint Extractor (static analysis)
purpose: For each MCP with fetchable source, extract the set of external hostnames it connects to via static analysis. This is the foundational data for endpoint trust (Phase III.b/c), threat intelligence (Phase IV.a), and domain provenance (Phase IV.b). Without this, all endpoint-based signals degrade to 'unknown'. Phase III.a of SENTINEL_ROADMAP_v2.md.

pilot_spec.description: Run against 15 hand-picked candidate MCPs whose endpoint sets are KNOWN in advance (from reading their documentation). This is a ground-truth validation — we know what endpoints each SHOULD emit, so we can measure precision and recall of the extractor. Write results to /home/workspace/zo_sentinel/fixes/pilot_endpoint_extractor_results.json including for each candidate: expected_endpoints, extracted_endpoints, false_positives, false_negatives, extraction_method_breakdown.
pilot_spec.candidate_selection: 15 hand-picked MCPs with diverse characteristics: (a) 5 Anthropic official servers — endpoints known from documentation (e.g., server-google-maps calls maps.googleapis.com). (b) 5 well-known community MCPs with published endpoint docs. (c) 5 MCPs where the endpoint is env-var configurable rather than hardcoded (tests whether we correctly flag 'user-configurable' vs 'baked-in').

ground_truth.note: Operator provides expected endpoints per candidate as a JSON input file before pilot run. Pilot reports precision/recall against this ground truth.

success_criteria: precision >= 80% on pilot candidates (extracted endpoints match expected)
zero false-positive hostnames resolving to test/localhost/example.com
extraction runtime under 60 seconds per MCP
source-fetching happens once per MCP and is cached
abort_conditions: recall < 50% — extraction strategy insufficient, needs operator review before scaling
precision < 60% — too much noise, rules need tightening
any MCP source fetch fails authentication (we should never hit private repos; pilot candidates are all public)
any MCP tarball exceeds 50MB — halt and reconsider strategy before engaging with large repos

extraction_strategy.description: Multi-method extraction with evidence per finding. Each hostname has a detection_method field so we can tune rules.

methods.name: url_literal_grep
methods.description: Regex for 'https?://[a-z0-9.-]+' in all source files. High recall, moderate precision.

methods.name: fetch_call_arg
methods.description: Parse AST/pattern-match for arg of fetch(), requests.get/post, axios.request, urllib.request.urlopen. Higher precision.

methods.name: config_default
methods.description: Extract default values in .env.example, config.json, config.ts, settings.py.

methods.name: readme_documented
methods.description: Parse README for 'connects to X' or 'API endpoint: Y' patterns. Lowest confidence but useful when code analysis finds nothing.

exclusions: schema.org, docs.npmjs.com, semver.org (schema refs, not endpoints)
github.com URLs pointing at the MCP's own repo (self-reference)
package.json registry refs (these are the npm package itself, not an outbound endpoint)

user_configurable_detection.heuristic: If a hostname only appears inside a process.env / os.getenv pattern, flag user_configurable=true. If it's both hardcoded AND env-overridable, flag baked_in_with_override=true. If only hardcoded, flag baked_in=true.

exported_functions.name: extract_endpoints
exported_functions.description: Run all extraction methods against a cloned/unpacked MCP source. Returns dict with endpoints (list of hostname objects), methods_used, source_stats.

exported_functions.name: fetch_mcp_source
exported_functions.description: Given a server_id, resolve its source (github clone OR npm tarball OR pypi tarball), cache locally. Returns path to extracted source.

mcp_source_cache_log.purpose: Track which source trees have been fetched and when, so we don't re-fetch unchanged ones

rate_limit_discipline.doctrine: Weekly extraction cycle in steady state. Source cache persists; we re-extract only when source changes.

source_fetch_limits.github: shallow clone depth=1, size cap 50MB per repo, respect GitHub API rate limits even for raw.githubusercontent fetches
source_fetch_limits.pypi: pypi.org source tarball, size cap 50MB, 1 req/second

rate_limit_discipline.cache_ttl: 7 days (sources change slowly); re-extract sooner only if fetcher detects a new version

forbidden: DO NOT execute any fetched source code — this is STATIC analysis only. No npm install, no pip install, no node/python invocation of MCP code.
DO NOT fetch private repos — public only, require the repo to be publicly accessible
DO NOT cache fetched source beyond 7 days — storage discipline
DO NOT write to mcp_endpoints without evidence_file and evidence_line populated — we need to audit every finding
DO NOT use /write endpoint for new tables — auto-id bug (Commit A lessons). Use /execute with explicit INSERT.
security_considerations: Fetched MCP source could be malicious. Extraction must happen in a read-only sandbox (no network during analysis, no code execution).
Some MCP sources contain credentials in example configs — endpoint extraction must strip credentials from evidence before writing to database.
Large tarballs could be a DoS vector — 50MB hard cap, timeout at 60 seconds per fetch.
acceptance_tests: extract_endpoints on a known flagship MCP returns at least the documented endpoints
extracting from same source twice produces identical results (deterministic)
URLs containing credentials (https://user:pass@host) are stripped to just the hostname
localhost and *.example.com are excluded from results
pilot ground-truth validation run completes with precision >=80%, recall >=70%
unlocks: Phase IV.a threat_intelligence_enrichment (which needs endpoints to check)
